chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'And for God upon people is the pilgrimage to the House, whoever is able to find a way to it.' He said: 'He goes out and walks, if he does not have what he rides.' I said: 'He cannot manage walking.' He said: 'He walks and rides.' I said: 'He cannot manage that, meaning walking.' He said: 'He serves the people and goes out with them.'

key_terms.يَرْكَبُ: He rides (on a beast of burden)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for fulfilling the obligation of Hajj if one cannot afford to ride or walk?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar elucidates the principle of 'tadaruj' (gradualism) in fulfilling the Hajj obligation, demonstrating how physical limitations are accommodated through a hierarchy of effort. It highlights the scholarly view that serving fellow pilgrims is not merely a supplementary act but a valid, primary mode of discharge for those unable to travel independently, reflecting the practical flexibility of Shia fiqh in applying the Quranic verse 'and upon Allah is the pilgrimage for those who can find a way.'
